acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Dragons family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Elder Wyrm, T4, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Hoardfall Roost Controller (Champion) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two water construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Ancient and immense, with wings broad enough to blot out the sun, torn and scarred membrane, thick chipped horns, and old gold coins fused visibly into the belly scales.

Signature mechanic: Hoardfall Roost: the Elder Wyrm rakes one coin-fused belly plate across a scarred wing spar, releasing a line of hot, heavy coins between a launch perch and landing mound. Younger Dragons use the line as a shared claim and circuit edge; the Wyrm guards it with one sun-blot wing sweep but cannot cover the torn trailing membrane.
battlefieldDuty: Control takeoff and landing zones by unfurling scarred sun-blocking wings and shedding fused belly coins into temporary roost lines that organize younger Dragons' movement.
constructionDimensions: Scale and breath anatomy become hydraulic through overlapping channel scales, finned horn gutters, throat pressure bladders, slick membrane ribs, and hoard-metal valves embedded along pale belly plates.

Surface and motion track coherent water volume through wet reflections, filling throat chambers, narrow tail-following jets, membrane runoff, mist only at pressure release, and visibly draining body channels.
counterplay: Cross through the visible membrane tear, scatter the coin line before lower Dragons establish claims, or strike the pale belly patch exposed where the fused hoard was shed. Affinity signal: The throat bladder swells and belly valves lift before a pressure action; striking an open valve drains the chamber and leaves the associated wing or jaw heavy.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only water treatment without channel scales, pressure organs, and wet material response
Glow-only water treatment without coherent reservoirs, valves, or flow direction
Shapeless water bodies that erase reptilian anatomy and age silhouette
Opaque spray that conceals flight lanes, throat pressure, or belly valves
identityInvariants: Long neck and tail, deep chest, four clawed limbs, wedge-shaped horned skull, and wings that emerge and expand after the wingless first form.
Each individual holds one coherent metallic or jewel-tone scale identity with a paler underbelly and bright reflective eyes, rather than changing base identity by affinity.
Overlapping scales, horn, bone spurs, and leathery wing membrane retain reptilian load paths and readable joints at every tier.
Horn crowns, spinal ridges, battle scars, torn membrane, and hoard metal fused into old belly scales accumulate as age and territorial history.
Wingspan and horn crown escalate together from absent wings and horn nubs to storm-front wings and branching imperial antlers, while the ground-to-sky grammar remains recognizable.
telegraph: Chipped horns lower, fused belly coins lift like scales, and sunlight appears through one old membrane tear as the massive wing stretches over the selected route.
